items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: my youngest sister, Madelyn, she became a very -- a hairdresser

ctx.x: of guys, they say, oh, my mother was a pianist. My father was this or that, my sister, but that never happened in my family. There was nobody musically inclined in my family. My mother was a very famous modiste, a woman that could copy any kind of clothes, like rich people see a beautiful gown in the paper, they would show it to my mother and she could duplicate it.

My father was a master electrician with his own gang working under him for the Pennsylvania Railroad and my sisters, they -- my youngest sister, Madelyn, she became a very -- a hairdresser and my oldest sister was a housekeeper, you know, for a coffee magnate here in New York. My little brother was just on the scene, comme si, comme sa. You know.

But me, when I was a kid, a teenager, I always liked to make money. I was out to make some kind of money. Well, a dollar was big money then, quarter, dime, I'd run errands for the grocery man. I would even run errands for the Chinaman in my town. I caddied when I was 14 years old, I caddied at a place, Deer Beach Country Club, which was very fashionable.
